A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Modular Duality in Deep Learning. Their sections, equations, Table 1, and references can be matched reliably. Neither PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v1 presents mathematical constructions and algorithms, without original empirical results. The NanoGPT speed record is attributed to Jordan (2024); Table 1 summarizes formulas rather than measurements.

after.justification: v2 likewise contains no original empirical evaluation. The retained NanoGPT speed-record discussion reports externally attributed work.

M1.justification: The atomic duality maps, module composition and concatenation rules, and Newton–Schulz procedures remain unchanged. Revised novelty and attribution statements do not change the algorithms.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks. The theoretical layer examples and references to external NanoGPT training remain unchanged in coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. Shampoo, maximal update parameterization, and alternative numerical methods remain subjects of theoretical comparison.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols, splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or error analyses. The conceptual comparisons of numerical methods are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No measured results are added or revised. The externally cited NanoGPT speed-record outcome remains unchanged, and Table 1 retains the same mathematical entries.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 narrows the general definition of a duality map from identification in either direction to a function from the dual space to the primal space, explicitly stating that it need not be an involution. The norm-based definition, Proposition 1, and subsequent derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v1 prominently claims a new rectangular Newton–Schulz iteration and novel GPU-friendly algorithms. v2 withdraws that algorithmic novelty claim and acknowledges earlier origins, substantially narrowing an advertised contribution. It also changes the abstract's NanoGPT attribution from 'our iteration' to a variant of the methods; the modular-dualization contribution remains.

C2.justification: The scientific interpretations and limitations remain: the proposed unification of Shampoo and maximal update parameterization, singular-value explanations, numerical-conditioning caveats, and batch-size qualification are unchanged. The provenance corrections do not introduce new mechanism explanations or limitations.

D1.justification: Initialization choices, polynomial-iteration guidance, and the proposed Modula testbed remain unchanged. The Higham equation reference is relocated within Section 5.3 rather than newly disclosed; no implementation resources or experimental details are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kovarik (1970) and Björck and Bowie (1971) and explicitly acknowledges the iteration's long history in Section 5.3. This materially repositions a claimed original algorithm as established prior work, rather than merely expanding the bibliography. The framework's relationship to other optimization research is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the abstract, duality-map terminology, attribution passages, and conclusion. Section 5.3 reorganizes the development-history explanation, but the overall section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption drops the claim of a newly proposed iteration family, while its structure and formulas remain unchanged. Section 5.3 spacing and reference pagination shift modestly; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scholarly accuracy by withdrawing the iteration's novelty claim and explicitly acknowledging its historical origins. The qualified NanoGPT attribution and clearer duality-map wording also improve precision. These are valuable, focused corrections; the central technical constructions and supporting evidence remain essentially unchanged.
